value: keyv / cacheable npm worm, a third-wave Shai-Hulud (Mini Shai-Hulud family) self-propagating supply-chain worm (Socket, SafeDep, Aikido, Wiz, 2026-08-04). The maintainer account 'Jaredwray' was compromised and used to publish trojanized versions across the keyv and cacheable package families, then the payload used stolen npm tokens + OIDC trusted publishing to republish hundreds more packages across at least nine organizations. Delivery is a package.json 'preinstall' hook (node setup.mjs) that downloads a standalone Bun 1.3.13 runtime and runs a ~728 KB Bun bundle (Math_Symbol.js) which harvests cloud/CI/dev credentials, republishes packages (worm), plants .claude/.vscode autostart hooks, and installs a host-level token-revocation dead-man's switch. Unattributed operator; family link to Shai-Hulud is medium confidence.
context: high

No CVE. This is a maintainer/package compromise (malicious published npm tarballs and a poisoned source tree), not a software vulnerability; absence from CISA KEV is expected and is not evidence of low risk.

value: Exfiltration avoids a fixed C2: a GitHubSender component creates repos via POST /user/repos and commits findings via the GraphQL createCommitOnBranch mutation, while a DomainSender resolves destinations via DNS and health-checks them before sending. All collected data is AES-256-GCM encrypted (12-byte IV, 16-byte tag) under an operator public key stored as an encrypted constant, so GitHub/DNS destinations receive only ciphertext.

value: Scale (2026-08-04, figures not fully reconcilable): SafeDep 1,684 poisoned versions across 420 package names tied to nine organizations, moving between orgs every 2-7 minutes; Aikido at least 868 packages across 1,381 versions. Totals count malicious artifacts, not victim systems. keyv 5.x line and the scoped @keyv/* adapters were reported clean; latest often re-resolved to a malicious version for other names, so upgrade-only may preserve exposure.
